newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: PRESS DIGEST - South Korean newspapers - June 5.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - South Korean newspapers - June 5.

text.p: The following is a summary of major stories in leading South Korean newspapers, prepared by Reuters in Seoul. Reuters has not checked the stories and does not guarantee their accuracy.

- Students were holed up in Hanyang University on Wednesday, after admitting to beating a man who later died in the latest twist in the year's most violent protests organised by a radical student group, Hanchongryon.

- President Kim Young-sam on Wednesday defended Lee Hoi-chang, chirman of the ruling New Korea Party, who is under pressure from his rival presidential hopefuls to step down, by saying that the party should unite under the leadership of chairman Lee.
- The composite stock price index fluctuated throughout Wednesday, and recorded the highest trade volume ever.
- North Korea's food crisis is over, except for some isolated regions where international aid packages cannot reach, the National Unification Ministry said.
- Private economic think tanks are rushing to forecast an earlier-then-expected recovery of the Korean economy.
